subject: Post-demo: TTFT acceptance criteria & streaming cadence confirmation
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie@aeroapps.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Miroslav Novak <miro@aeroapps.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming targets from today's demo

Thanks for the demo earlier — great walkthrough. Below is a short recap from our side and the acceptance criteria we discussed so we can align on a pilot. Attaching our internal SLA spreadsheet (AeroApps_TTFT_SLA_v1.xlsx).

Quick recap / acceptance asks:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target median <= 80ms for short prompts (~<150 tokens), p95 <= 200ms.
- Throughput: target sustained 150 requests/sec, with short bursts to 300 rps for up to 5 minutes.
- Concurrency: expected concurrent sessions ~50 during peak.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for browser clients; chunk cadence: either 60-120 tokens or every ~200ms of generated output (whichever comes first). WebSocket fallback acceptable for mobile clients.
- Fallbacks: automatic model-variant fallback if primary model fails to meet latency SLOs; must be seamless to client.
- Telemetry: need request-level latency and per-chunk timestamps, plus token counts.

Open items we flagged on the call:
1) Warm vs cold: what warm-up profile do you need to meet p95?
2) Priming/long-context impacts on TTFT assumptions (how do primed prompts shift p95?)
3) Failure modes: graceful degradation plan and SDK guidance for chunk reassembly.

Proposed pilot: 24–72 hour pilot focused on our most common prompt shapes (we'll share sample payloads), aiming for 24h at 10–20 rps to validate instrumentation + TTFT profile, then scale.

Thanks — can you confirm whether Redwood can capture per-chunk timestamps and a sample instrumentation dashboard for this pilot?

—Jamie
Senior Platform Engineer, AeroApps

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 12:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming targets from today's demo

Jamie — thanks for the clear recap and the SLA file. This is very helpful. High-level answers and clarifying questions below; I also attached the demo recording for your team to reference (demo-recording-20260801.mp4).

Short answers:
- Per-chunk timestamps: yes — Redwood can emit per-chunk events with millisecond timestamps in telemetry. We can expose these in a pilot dashboard (token-level timing + end-to-end request timeline).
- SSE vs WebSocket: SSE is supported and will be our recommended path for browser clients; WebSocket fallback is straightforward for mobile apps.
- Model fallback: we have routing policies to fallback to compatible model variants and can do automatic rollbacks / canary routing to limit blast radius.

Clarifying questions to size the pilot and engineering work:
1) For the 150 rps steady-state target: is that peak for a single region or global? If global, please provide per-region distribution.
2) Do you have representative prompt length distribution (percentile tokens) and average response size? We need those to estimate KV-cache pressure and batching efficacy.
3) Do you expect long context windows with priming for all traffic or a small subset?
4) Any hard constraints on p95 outages / acceptable retry behavior?

Pilot proposal (from Redwood):
- Phase 1 (Sanity): 24 hours at 10–20 rps using a reserved Dedicated pool to validate telemetry, chunk timestamps, and TTFT measurements.
- Phase 2 (Scale): 48–72 hours ramp to 150 rps steady-state with short burst tests to 300 rps. We’ll instrument per-route dashboards and a Canary route for model fallback verification.

Next steps I suggest: you share sample payloads + traffic distribution; we’ll spin up a dedicated pilot and provide a lightweight dashboard within 48 hours of data. Can we target the week of Aug 10 for the pilot?

Thanks — looping in Ben Carter (Sales Eng) and Karthik Iyer (Inference Eng) for a quick alignment on capacity and kernel/quantization questions.

—Sofia

Forwarding AeroApps' SLA and my reply — summary below and asks.

Summary of their targets:
- TTFT median <=80ms, p95 <=200ms for short prompts
- 150 rps steady-state (bursts to 300 rps), concurrency ~50
- SSE primary, chunk cadence ~60–120 tokens or ~200ms; WS fallback

Asks for sync:
- Ben: can we propose a Dedicated pool sizing and an initial cost estimate for a pilot that covers Phase 1 (10–20 rps) and Phase 2 ramp to 150 rps? Also want wording for the pilot agreement that limits risk (automatic rollback, canary config).
- Karthik: any immediate concerns on model variant choices, quantization profile, or kernel-level warm-up strategies to hit p95? They will send sample payloads soon; they also want per-chunk timestamps and token-level telemetry.

Proposed timeline: target pilot kickoff the week of Aug 10. AeroApps is US-based; assume single-region (us-west) unless they confirm otherwise.

Please reply with capacity/cost and any technical caveats by Monday EOD so I can get back to them with a concrete pilot plan.

—Sofia
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming targets from today's demo

Thanks for the forward. Quick responses and next steps from Sales Eng perspective.

Capacity & cost (initial pilot estimate):
- Phase 1 (10–20 rps, 24h): we can run this on a small Dedicated pool (2x A100-class equivalent) — estimated incremental cost covered under our pilot program; I'll confirm credits we can apply.
- Phase 2 ramp (up to 150 rps steady, burst to 300 rps): recommend a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with autoscale headroom + warm standby. Estimated commit for 72 hours: will provide a ballpark $ figure in a separate note once Karthik confirms memory/quant choices.

Technical caveats:
- Warmstart: to meet p95 for short prompts reliably we'll want a warm cache and KV priming. If AeroApps runs long-context primed flows for a significant fraction, p95 will increase — we should quantify after sample payloads.
- Chunk cadence: 200ms cadence is achievable, but actual tokens-per-chunk depends on model throughput. We'll provide guidance to tune chunk-size vs latency tradeoffs in the pilot.
- Telemetry: we can expose per-chunk timestamps and an early pilot dashboard; ensure they pass us sample payloads so telemetry dimensions align.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Sofia — ask AeroApps to share sample traffic (top 10 prompt templates + token sizes) and confirm region.
2) Karthik — can you advise on quantization and expected per-GPU throughput for the model family they indicated (we discussed a 30B-class open model)? If quantization to int8 or nf4 changes throughput significantly, we need to flag.
3) I’ll prepare a short pilot commitment email (scope, duration, rollback policy, data handling) we can send once we have samples.

I can join the kickoff sync on Aug 10 if needed.
